data.title: Alibaba Non-GAAP EPADS of $1.21 misses by $0.44, revenue of $40.5B in-line
data.description:
• Alibaba press release (BABA): Q2 Non-GAAP EPADS of $1.21 misses by $0.44.
  • Revenue of $40.5B (+10% Y/Y) in-line.
  • Adjusted EBITA, a non-GAAP measurement, increased 260% year-over-year to RMB32,636 million (US$4,868 million).
  • Net cash provided by operating activities was RMB15,690 million (US$2,340 million), an increase of 55% compared to RMB10,099 million in the same quarter of 2025.
  • Free cash flow, a non-GAAP measurement of liquidity, was an outflow of RMB34,472 million (US$5,142 million), compared to an outflow of RMB21,840 million in the same quarter of 2025.

data.title: Halma plc Non-GAAP EPS of 66.24p, revenue of £1.43B
data.description:
• Halma plc press release (HLMAF): 1H Non-GAAP EPS of 66.24p.
  • Revenue of £1.43B (+15.3% Y/Y).
  • Adjusted EBIT of £345.4M

  • Outlook for the 2027 financial year

     

    We have made a good start to the second half of the year. The strength of our first half performance means we are well placed to deliver our existing guidance for the 2027 financial year.

    While our companies continue to experience varied conditions in their end markets and economic and geopolitical uncertainty remains elevated, we continue to expect to deliver, for the year as a whole, low double-digit percentage organic7 constant currency revenue growth. This guidance includes premium9 growth of approximately five percentage points from our photonics business, implying an organic7 constant currency photonics growth rate of approximately 30%. Adjusted EBIT margin2 is expected to be in the range of 23.5% to 24%.

data.title: Jacobs tapped by Sanofi for Frankfurt insulin facility
data.description:
• Jacobs (J) has been selected by Sanofi (SNY) as the Engineering, Procurement and Construction Management (EPCM) partner for a new insulin manufacturing facility in Frankfurt, Germany.
  • Located alongside Sanofi’s established insulin manufacturing campus, the facility will support the production of multiple insulin products and strengthen supply reliability, according to a statement.
  • Jacobs will provide integrated EPCM services spanning design, procurement, construction management and commissioning. 
  • Shares in Jacobs (J) up marginally premarket.

data.title: U.S. futures climb as investors turn attention to Anthropic IPO
data.description:
U.S. stock futures moved higher early Thursday, with technology shares leading the gains, as investors turned their attention to the highly anticipated public debut of artificial intelligence startup Anthropic.

Nasdaq 100 futures (US100:IND) jumped +1.86%, S&P 500 futures (SPX) gained +1.09%, and Dow Jones Industrial Average futures (INDU) advanced +0.67%.

Anthropic, the company behind the Claude AI chatbot, is set to begin trading on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT after pricing its IPO at $83 a share, above its expected range. The company raised approximately $81.3 billion, and its debut could offer a gauge of how public-market investors are assessing the longer-term commercial prospects of AI amid recent weakness in several AI-linked stocks.

Traders will also monitor weekly jobless claims and quarterly results from Walmart (WMT) before the opening bell.

U.S. Treasury yields edged higher across the curve. The 2-year Treasury yield (US2Y) rose 0.9 basis points to 4.82%, the 5-year yield climbed 0.9 basis points to 4.90%, and the benchmark 10-year Treasury yield (US10Y) ticked up 0.2 basis points to 5.08%. The 30-year yield (US30Y) increased 0.6 basis points to 5.42%.

Top gainers included State Street (STT) +16.48%, Palo Alto Networks (PANW) +10.03%, and CrowdStrike (CRWD) +6.69%. Decliners included DTE Energy (DTE) -8.36%, Sysco (SYY) -1.85%, and Monster Beverage (MNST) -1.56%.

data.title: Wall Street $500B financing pledge for Nvidia fails to materialize- report
data.description:
A pledge from firms to secure $500B in financing for Nvidia (NVDA) chips, secured by Jensen Huang earlier this year, has failed to materialize, according to a Wall Street Journal report.

Huang, who left the chipmaking giant after a slew of extramarital affairs, got pledges from Apollo Global Management (APO), Blackstone (BX), BlackRock (BLK), Brookfield Asset Management (BAM), Goldman Sachs (GS) and KKR (KKR) in August.

The money would go to Nvidia customers, including OpenAI (OPENAI) and Anthropic (ANT) as well as smaller ones to buy the chips they needed.

However, no capital has been deployed, WSJ said, citing unnamed sources, and investor doubt is creeping in about whether the program will actually pan out, especially with Huang’s exit and the cautious approach of finance head and current interim CEO Colette Kress.

 “We are rigorously evaluating future investments, commitments and guarantees,” Kress said on Tuesday on Nvidia’s earnings call.

data.title: Germany, France lead European gains as UK market trades near six-week low
data.description:
London (UKX) -0.06%, trading near a six-week low after three consecutive sessions of losses, as gains in banking, mining and defence stocks were offset by weakness in consumer-facing stocks.

Germany (DAX:IND) +0.80%.

France (CAC:IND) +0.55%. 

In other parts of Europe, industrial production in Switzerland rose by 0.8% Y/Y in Q3. Switzerland’s trade surplus widened to CHF 3.2B in October.

The Netherlands' seasonally adjusted unemployment rate remained unchanged at 4.0% in October.

The pan-European Stoxx 600 (STOXX) moved 0.43% higher to 647, reversing losses from the previous four trading sessions. Market sentiment was lifted by Anthropic’s (ANT) $83-per-share IPO pricing, which marked the largest initial public offering on record.

In the bond market, the U.S. 10-year bond was up 1 basis point to 5.08%.

UK's 10-year yield was up 1 basis points to 5.30%.

Germany's 10-year yield was down 1 basis points to 3.37%.
